utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you, Mr. Lemal, of the affirmation you took at the commencement of your evidence which still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lemal.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lemal, yesterday you testified that you were commended for your role of the evacuation of casualties which took place in the combat activities that were carried out on 23rd October; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And these combat activities in which your battalion commander Captain Ekrem Delic and others were wounded were in fact planned -- a planned operation of the 2nd Operational Group which was carried out with units of the 2nd Operational Group including the 3rd Battalion with the object of capturing territory. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't an operation. It was a planned reconnoitering which is done on a regular basis in front of the front lines, and this happened 300 or 400 metres in front of our front lines. And this could not have been planned because it was a group of four or five men, and none of us subordinates was aware of this undertaking or, rather, this action by the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So your position is that -- let me withdraw that. Are you aware that there was a planned combat operation carried out by forces of the 2nd Operational Group including the 3rd Battalion in the period 23rd to 25th October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware because I was wounded on the 23rd of October. So I was hospitalised.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown document P121, that is tab 21 of Jokic binder, as well as P119, tab 19 of Jokic binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, I'm going to show you two documents that have been tendered in evidence before this Trial Chamber. Could you first examine the document titled P121, which is dated 23 October 1991. Now, doesn't that clearly reflect that on 23 October 1991 the 3rd Battalion was participating in fact in a combat operation, and in fact your participation in the evacuation of the wounded on 23rd October was pursuant to this particular order?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, this is an order dated the 23rd of October for action on the 24th, if you read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may point out the particular paragraph. In the English version under the subtitle 472nd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: "The 3rd Motorised Battalion should before dawn try to pull out the wounded soldiers whereas the forwarded part of the unit should be extracted to the relevant front line positions Ivanica, Harastica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Why do you say that was before dawn on the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, my point is that this is before dawn on the 24th; that is correct. But my point is that this document indicates clearly that there was a planned combat operation going on in the course of which the casualties were taken, which this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's your problem. In the course of which. Is not this exercise carried out during the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me go on to -- perhaps if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I may misunderstand the evidence, but I understood that it was on the 23rd of October that the action occurred in which -- or in respect of which Mr. Lemal was decorated.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But this document shows that before dawn on 24th, the 3rd Battalion is to evacuate the soldiers and that it is pursuant to this order that the 3rd -- units of the 3rd Battalion evacuated the soldiers, the casualties. That is my point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if that's your point, be aware that I understand the evidence a day differently from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So perhaps moving on from there in view of the views expressed by the Chamber, the Trial Chamber, could you please indicate as to who has issued this order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order to pull out the wounded commander I received from the then deputy captain Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question to you, Mr. Lemal, is: Who has issued this order which you are holding right now, this written order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This written order was issued by the command of the 2nd Operational Group, but it was signed on behalf of General Strugar by somebody whose signature I do not recognise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, I did not ask you all those details, but as to which command has issued this order. Could you please examine document number P119, the order dated 24 October 1991. Can you please look at the last page of the order and indicate as to who has issued this particular combat order.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to underline that as of the afternoon of the 23rd, I was no longer in the unit. I was at the hospital in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, my question was very straightforward. It was as to who has issued this order which is now before you. It has nothing to do with whether you were there or not. Do you find it difficult to respond to that question?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't find it difficult. This order, without a signature, was issued by the commander, Lieutenant Colonel Pavle Strugar, but there is no signature on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And in his capacity as the commander of the 2nd Operational Group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But I don't know how valid this order is if it's not signed. There is no signature by General Strugar here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, the validity of this order will be decided by the Trial Chamber. Please respond to my questions. Now, do you see that these two orders are in fact combat orders issued by the command of the 2nd Operational Group which issues directions to the 472nd Motorised Brigade to which your battalion, the 3rd Battalion, belonged to at this time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In fact, by P -- document dated 23 October 1991, which is P121, it specifically assigns tasks to the 3rd Battalion, and I'm referring to paragraph which is titled under 472nd Motorised Brigade, the second paragraph which states: "3rd Motorised Battalion should before dawn try to pull out the wounded soldiers whereas the forwarded part of the unit should be extracted to the relevant front line positions." So specific tasks are assigned to the 3rd Battalion, your battalion, by the 2nd Operational Group command; correct? By this order.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say to pull out the wounded, because I pulled out the wounded on the 23rd. Here it says to pull out the dead who were still left at those positions, because those who survived I pulled out on the 23rd, and some of the dead, but some of the dead stayed behind, and that was what the unit was tasked on the 24th, to pull out the remaining dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and I really appreciate if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you could confine your response to the question. My question is: Does this order assign specific tasks to the 3rd Motorised Battalion? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you, being a company commander of the 3rd Battalion until 1992, you did not -- you were not aware of a formation --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection, because my learned friend insists on leaving out what the document says, and it is a document from the command of the 2nd Operational Group addressed to the command of the 9th VPS and the 472nd Brigade. She seems to imply that there is a direct relationship is simply not true, and it doesn't follow from this document. It is not an order from the 2nd Operational Group to the 3rd Battalion but an order from the 2nd Operational Group to the command of the VPS. That is what it says clearly in the first row of this document, and that should be reflected in the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And also to the command of the 472nd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the 3rd Motorised, we understand that the "brigade" should read "battalion" further down was to try to pull out a wounded soldier, or the wounded soldier, if the English translation is correct, rather than soldiers or dead, but nevertheless. Having got what the document says a little more clearly, your question was whether this was an order to the 472nd Motorised Brigade from the 2nd Operational Group allocating tasks to battalions of the 472nd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your answer, Mr. Lemal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But in the order it clearly says to pull out the killed soldier. That is what it says in the order, and not the wounded, because I pulled out the wounded on the 23rd. Just one dead soldier was left behind, Miroslav Anusic, who was to be pulled out on that day, 24th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. That appears as though it may be a problem with the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, in view of these documents isn't it -- may I rephrase. Your position is that until February 1992, you were not aware of the formation named the 2nd Operational Group. Now, being a company commander of the 3rd Battalion, it is clear from these documents that the 3rd Battalion has participated in combat operations based on orders issued by the 2nd Operational Group, but notwithstanding that, until February 1992, you were not aware of the 2nd Operational Group. Isn't that -- isn't that unacceptable?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know why. I was just a company commander. Then there's battalion commander, then brigade commander, then the commander of the VPS, then the commander of the 2nd Operational Group. That is five steps up from me in the hierarchy. So I don't see why I should know and be familiar with more than one to two steps up the chain of command, and that is what the regulations say anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, you attended, you said, regular briefings with your battalion commander, did you not? That was your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... regular briefings, didn't you ever hear the term or the mention of the 2nd Operational Group? Such as there is a combat order from the 2nd Operational Group which has been passed down to us or something to that effect being mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The VPS was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown D98.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, you were shown this document yesterday, and you asked to respond to -- explain certain items listed there. Do you see that this daily report is also forwarded to the 2nd Operational Group command in addition to the 9th VPS forward command post in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, again evidence is interpreted in a way that is not correct. I appeal to my learned friend to interpret the document correctly. It is addressed to the command of the operational group. So could there be a little more attention paid to the specifics of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The document is addressed to the command of the 2nd Operational Group and the command of the military naval district, VP command post IKM. That's what I just read. I don't know what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 8, in line 13, you said it was forwarded to the 2nd Operational Group and the 9th VPS forward command post in Kupari. So please look at what you said on page 8, line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I will remind counsel that they will stop addressing each other directly. You will speak to the Bench. We've fallen back into this unfortunate habit of direct address to each other when there are objections. That will and can lead to unpleasant personal relationships. You will put your submissions impartially to the Bench, and we will deal with the matter. It is correct, as Mr. Petrovic has said, that you did in one or two matters misquote the document. Whether they are material is another matter. But it is addressed to the command of the military naval district at the command post, as you have indicated. It is also addressed to the command of the 2nd Operational Group. I think we've got that clear, and if you would carry on from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please accept my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, going back to your testimony on 6th December. Now, you testified that on 5th December you were ordered by Captain Kovacevic to record to Ivanica. What time did you receive this -- these instructions from Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I received the instructions from Captain Kovacevic but from the command post of the battalion. I received an order to report to the command post held by Captain Jeremic at Ivanica and that we should wait for him there, wait for Captain Kovacevic until he comes back from reporting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, your testimony is that Captain Kovacevic instructed you to report to Ivanica unless you want to correct it right now. My question is: At what time did you receive these instructions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the testimony of this witness is being misquoted. Could we please be told where the witness made this statement, that is, that he received the order directly from Kovacevic to go to Captain Jeremic's command post. Could we be told where the reference is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Ms. Mahindaratne. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I? At 140908, the question goes: "Let me interrupt you. When you say the command post can you be more precise. Answer, at 1419: "I got a call from Captain Kovacevic who was in Gornji Brgat." I'm referring to that command post. "I received an order to report to the command post of Captain Jeremic in Ivanica, and we were to wait there for the arrival of our commander from a briefing." So clearly the witness has testified, "I got a call from Captain Kovacevic who was in Gornji" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think that deals with that concern. Now your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, my question is: At what time did you received these instructions from Captain Kovacevic to report to Ivanica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to repeat that Captain Kovacevic did not give me that order. I received the order from his command post at Gornji Brgat that I shouldn't go there but instead to the Ivanica village, and it was early evening when the order arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: All right. Then at what time did you say -- whoever you received these instructions from, at what time did you receive these instructions? That's my question. Can you give a time? You said early evening. Approximate time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was already dark, so I can't be precise, but shall we say about 1800 hours approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And at what time were you to report to Ivanica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you we were told to go there immediately, all of us, so no time was given that we should go there straight away and wait for him there, which means that we could wait for him up until midnight. So as I was in Cajkovici, I got into my car and headed there, and by road it takes about 20 or so minutes to get there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you were in Cajkovici at the time you received that telephone call?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And accordingly did you immediately go to Ivanica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost immediately. Five to ten minutes later, which is the time it took me to issue commander's -- orders to the commander of the platoon, and then I set off for Ivanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you arrived there, was Captain Kovacevic there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When did he arrive?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He arrived straight after me, maybe five to ten minutes later.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when you arrived there, who else was present?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the commanders were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In examination in --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they were closer than I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In examination-in-chief, you testified that when you arrived there Captain Kovacevic was not there and the meeting started in his absence. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I arrived before him, but the meeting couldn't start without him. How could we work without him? So I didn't say we started the meeting. I just said that we were all there already.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me read back to you what you said yesterday, Mr. Lemal. This is at 141013. The question goes from Defence counsel: "Did you see him before you started your meeting? No. I didn't see him before we started our meeting. He arrived after us." That is your response. So, according to your response, clearly you started the meeting before you arrived. This is your testimony, Mr. Lemal, which I have read back to you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say that we started the meeting at all. I just said that we had all gathered there before him, before he arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well. You say that it took about five or ten minutes for him to arrive. Now, in examination-in-chief, you stated that you met him at the crossroad -- you saw his vehicle at the crossroad in Gornji Brgat coming from the route Kupari, Dubac, Gornji Brgat, Ivanica. So clearly his vehicle was right behind you then, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the road right up to Kupari, but in terms of kilometres I can't tell you exactly, but it would be certainly five or six kilometres or more going uphill.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, when you said that you saw Captain Kovacevic's vehicle at the intersection in Gornji Brgat, how far down the road was it? How did you -- was it close to you? Was it right behind you? Did you see exactly at that intersection?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't close. It was from the Dubac crossroads, that area, and it was the only vehicle going behind me and that stopped at Ivanica behind me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So clearly then he -- his vehicle came closely behind your vehicle. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't say it went straight behind me because if you look at the map you can see the distance between the crossroads at Gornji Brgat and the crossroads at Dubac.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, if one were to travel to Ivanica from Gornji Brgat, the route he would have to take is that route, isn't it, Gornji Brgat, Ivanica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So, however, the fact that that road leads beyond Gornji Brgat to Kupari leads you to conclude that he's coming from Kupari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In fact, even if he were to travel to Ivanica from Gornji Brgat, his command post, he would still have to take the same road as you just said.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Gornji Brgat is in fact closer to Ivanica than Kupari. Kupari is way beyond Gornji Brgat on that same road?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gornji Brgat is closer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying. Gornji Brgat is closer to Ivanica than Kupari. So he could --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If he was travelling from Gornji Brgat to Ivanica, he would be coming on that route. But nevertheless, based on the fact that he's on a route that also leads to Kupari makes you arrive at the conclusion that he's in fact coming from Kupari. You in fact -- you in fact have no basis to conclude that he was coming from Kupari although you -- you testified to such effect before this Trial Chamber. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the vehicle, the only vehicle. It was night-time. It was the only vehicle on the road from the Dubac crossroad, and I was at the crossroads at Gornji Brgat. When I arrived to in front of the Jeremic command post, I got out of my Pinzgauer vehicle. I looked around in the direction downwards, and that vehicle was already passing the crossroads at Gornji Brgat. I went inside with the other commanders and I said, "The chief is just coming." And several minutes later, he entered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... interrupt. My point is that you have no basis to conclude that Captain Kovacevic was in fact at that time travelling from Kupari, because it is the same route he would have to take even if he was travelling from Gornji Brgat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, would you leave the objection. The witness is dealing with the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I've already put the question to the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I answered your question to the best of my knowledge, like it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will move on. Now, was the deputy commander, Captain Soldo, present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And for how long did the meeting proceed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say in terms of time, but roughly about one and a half to two hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, according to what was planned, when your assault group from Strincjera was to approach the search facility, were you supposed to be given mortar fire support?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Ivanica, from Captain Jeremic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And how about Captain Pesic's group? From where were they to obtain their fire support?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Pesic, the same thing with him. It was the battery that supported both, because the Srdj facility is a relatively small one. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What time was it when the ZIS guns and the mortar fire on Srdj from their support positions started firing on 6th December? And now I'm going on to the attack itself.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what time was it when you got close to Srdj? That's the time when you signalled for the artillery fire to stop for the sake of the safety of your own troops.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was already about 8.00 when I grew closer to the repeater station, and at that point the mortar fire stopped from Isovo [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So from 6.00 to 8.00 your mortar fire support positions had been firing in the course of this attack.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And by 6.00 when your heavy weapons, the ZIS guns and the mortar fire started, your infantry group or the assault groups would have reached a particular point on Srdj. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at Srdj but the approach to Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you halfway up the hill or were you at the base when they started fire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left at 5.00 in the morning, and under the cover of darkness I managed to traverse that area without any fire, but after the mortar fire started at 6.00, I continued on my way. So when I was at a distance of 600 metres from the repeater, the firing stopped. And that was 8.00 roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What time was it when you entered the fort, when your group and Captain Pesic's group entered the fort on top of the Srdj hill?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Lieutenant Pesic entered a little bit before me. I entered roughly at about half past 8.00. I can't give you the exact time, but I think it was thereabouts. It took me another half hour to enter the repeater itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what time was it when the Croat guns from Lapad started firing at Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were at the repeater station itself for another half hour, and we were launching the fighting with the Croatian soldiers up there with -- until they left into the underground channels. So it was after that that the mortars started firing from Dubrovnik at the repeater station at Srdj itself. I can't tell you exactly what time that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could you give an approximate time? Now you said you entered the fort at 8.30. So about half hour after that, is that what you're saying, around 9.00?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, half an hour to one hour let's say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You stated that as a result of this fire from Lapad your units took some casualties. Now, were these the first casualties taken in this particular attack carried out on 6th December, 1991? First casualties amongst your units, the JNA units.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I lost a soldier in the approach to the repeater station.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What time was that when you -- when the soldier was killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, between 8.00 and half past 8.00 when we didn't have mortar fire support from our side. When I started out towards the repeater one soldier was hit by a sniper and he succumbed to his wounds. He died.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So that was the first loss in this particular attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what time was it when you started taking in more casualties at the top of Srdj as a result of the fire from Lapad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would make it roughly from between 11.00 -- actually, from 11.00 onwards. That general period was when the casualties fell at the call-out cell, the fort at Srdj and the repeater station there. I can't give you an exact time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: How long did it take you to withdraw from Srdj to Strincjera when Captain Kovacevic ordered you to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I withdrew -- it took me about an hour to an hour and a half. We were moving slowly in groups and carrying the dead, and I had some wounded soldiers too.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In the course of this withdrawal or while you were up there, did you hear that there had been an order to cease fire around 11.00 in the morning or about that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that there was an order to that effect. I wasn't informed that there was an order for a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In the course of the day did you receive a single order to cease fire, and if so, at what time was that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just received the order for withdrawal from Captain Kovacevic in the afternoon hours, and I carried out that. That's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So as far as you're concerned, there was no order for cease fire, to cease fire entirely on 6 December 1991, which was --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to me, no. It wasn't transmitted to me, no. The only order I received was the one I told you about, the order to withdrawal, and that order implied a cease-fire too. So withdrawal to initial positions, original positions, implies that, and I received no other order.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you stated that there was a protest among -- amongst your units that -- on the basis that the men were killed because the promised artillery fire was not provided. Is that a reference to the 130-millimetre cannons in Cilipi that was not provided in the course of this attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because that was what was promised at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And that promise was conveyed to you by Captain Kovacevic. He said that these artillery would be provided in the course of the attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: After the 6th December events, did you hear in fact Captain Kovacevic blame this fact - that is to say, the refusal to provide artillery fire from Cilipi - being the reason for the failure to take Srdj in the attack? Did you hear him blaming that, for instance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me that on the same day, the 6th of December in the afternoon when he came to see me. And when I asked him, "What's all this, why weren't we given fire support?" And he said that he didn't know and that was the reason for everything that followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you also, in speaking with Captain Kovacevic that evening or perhaps the next day or the day thereafter, did you hear him telling Captain Nesic, that is the commander of the anti-armour company, that he all used his artillery fire which resulted in too much of damage to the town for which Captain Kovacevic was concerned that they might be held accountable? Did you hear Captain Kovacevic say anything to this effect?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not hear anything like that. And at official meetings that was never brought up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you at any meeting thereafter hear Captain Nesic being congratulated for what was considered as a very good shot at the Srdj cross which destroyed the cross? Did you hear anything to such effect?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you meet Captain Kovacevic on the 7th December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: How about other company commanders of the battalion? Did you meet them on the 7th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anybody. I was at Strincjera up until noon, and in the afternoon I was in Cajkovici. So it was just passing by the command post that I informed that I -- them that I was going from Strincjera to Cajkovici, and there is no command post there or any commander of a company there. So I didn't see anybody on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: How about the day after, the 7th or the 8th December?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th, I went to attend a funeral of a soldier Divljan who had been killed near Gacko at the village of Kravjani [phoen]. Of course having received permission from my commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And there did you meet any of the other company commanders of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Was there ever a meeting held at the command post in Brgat, command post of the 3rd Battalion, after the 6th of December, any time Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. after the 6th of December, where the 6th December events were analysed and discussed between the 3rd Battalion command personnel as well as the company commanders, including yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: A meeting was held, but I don't really know the time. And, yes, there was an analysis, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When was that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I don't know exactly when it was. I can't remember the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Was it close to the 6th December? A month after, a week after?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't on the 6th certainly. As to the rest, I really can't say. I don't know. I can't be specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And who was present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Present were all the company commanders, the battalion commander, and members of the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And at this meeting, did you hear Captain Kovacevic blame Captain Nesic for all using his artillery which caused too much of damage to the town for which he expressed his concern that they would be held accountable?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some words, but I really can't remember now because I was focussed on my unit. However, there were some words of criticism addressed at Nesic, but what he was criticised for specifically I don't know. But he was the person most criticised.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And criticised by Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: For the role he played in the 6th December attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he was criticised most, but I didn't pay much attention to the reasons why he was being criticised. Most probably because of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And in the course of the 6th December attack, Captain Nesic was commanding his unit from Zarkovica, the anti-armour unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: On 6th December, did officers of the 9th VPS visit you after the incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And did they ask you what happened, and did you discuss the events with them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did talk to them, but I don't remember who was there of them, whether it was Zarkovic or Sofronije or which of them. One of the two was there. They first asked what the situation was with respect to the manpower, what the morale was, did -- were there any problems with the men, and I informed them. I said there was no artillery fire support from Cilipi, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Sir, do you know the first name of the person you mentioned as Sofronije? I beg your pardon. Just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Just going back to a point, Mr. Lemal, going back, in fact, to the 5th December. You said that you were asked to meet or report to Captain Jeremic's post. Can you -- do you know what his first name is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatan.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you -- you were on the point of what you discussed with the officers of the 9th VPS on 6th December when they visited your position after the attack. Did you also give them a verbal report of what really occurred? And I'm not talking about a written report. I'm talking about a verbal report.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did they take down notes or did they write down your version anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. They didn't write down anything. At least not then at the facility at Strincjera.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Where did they write it down, or did you write down this report and pass it on to them, or did they write it down at any other place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they wrote anything down, but on the spot I reported to them about what had happened and how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: At any point of time after the 6th December did you submit a written report of your combat activity either to Captain Kovacevic or his superior command, or any officers of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except for that piece of reporting. Nobody ever asked me any written report or written explanation about those events.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, are you not required to submit daily combat reports after an operation or, if it's not daily, regular combat reports?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not done at the company level. This is done at higher levels.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So for higher levels to submit combat reports to their higher levels, would you not have to in fact - in writing or even verbally - report to your battalion commander as to the combat activity that your unit was responsible for the day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you that I did submit my report, that the commander visited me on the 6th in the afternoon. I told him what had happened, how many losses I had had, what ammunition I had used. I also asked him how come there was no artillery support from Cilipi. And the case there wasn't any was the direct cause of the death of two of my soldiers. He told me he didn't know. And in my view this was my official report to him regarding the combat activities that had taken place on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you did submit a report to your -- to Captain Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, after the 6th December operation, did you recommend or propose the names of any of your soldiers or officers for decoration for their role in the attack, and did you, for instance, propose the names of deceased soldiers for decoration posthumously?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for the 6th of December. I did not recommend anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But you did in fact do so with regard to the normal combat activity where you were not even present to witness their bravery, but not in this instance. Why not? Was there any particular difficulty attached to this particular combat operations which did not allow you to, for instance, propose anyone for decoration?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference between the two operations. In the first one, we took the territory. There were no casualties. In the second, we failed in our mission, and there were casualties. In my view, the second mission was failed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And also in this particular instance the Old Town [Realtime transcript read in error "whole town"] was shelled. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I heard, and subsequently I also saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have a problem with the interpretation. My learned friend said the whole town was shelled, and in the B/C/S the interpretation was the Old Town was shelled. The interpretation in B/C/S was the Old Town, whereas my learned friend did not use the words "the Old Town" according to what I'm reading in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I used the word "Old Town," not "whole town." Stari Grad. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. On page 25, line 1, it says "the whole town." I was reading the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And so you did hear and you said you also saw it subsequently that Stari Grad, the Old Town, was shelled.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I couldn't see it on that day because of the repeater station and because of the combat activities that were under way. It was only subsequently that I saw that some of the parts of the Old Town had been hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And you observed the damage? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that some roofs were damaged and that there was other damage on the houses in the Old Town that had been hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lemal, you testified in examination-in-chief that you heard in the course of briefings, the regular briefings that were conducted at the battalion command, Captain Nesic and Stojanovic protest to Captain Kovacevic about receiving fire from the Old Town. When was this? When did you hear this? Can you give the time frames?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between mid-November when I returned to my unit and the 6th of December when we carried out the attack on Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And can you -- how many times did you hear that between mid-November and 6th December?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few times. I heard it a few times.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And do you know what Captain Kovacevic did about those protests?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that he would convey this to his superior command when he went to the briefings in Kupari. He also said that he would insist with them for these things to stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You referred to Captain Nesic complaining of sniper fire from the houses around hotels. Now, what are those hotels? Can you name them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is only one name I'm aware of and that is Argentina. I don't know the names of the others. I know that there are two hotels, but I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And those are hotels which are outside the Old Town, to the east of the Old Town, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are outside the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you also said that you heard Captain Nesic complain of an anti-aircraft 20-millimetre weapon in relation to the Old Town. Did he mention where exactly it was located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He mentioned a fort or a fortress in the Old Town but I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly which one. He mentioned a fortress on top of which an anti-aircraft 20-millimetre gun was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when was this? Can you approximately give the time period? Now, you said this was between November and the 6th December. Was it late November, around the 20th, the last week of November, the first week of December? What? Could you give some idea as to the time frame?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I can't be more precise than that. It was between mid-November and the 6th of December. I can't be any more precise than that, and I couldn't be any more specific about the dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown D65.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, the document that you're about to be shown is a document tendered by the Defence on behalf of General Strugar and is in evidence before the Trial Chamber. This document is titled "Action report of the 3rd Battalion on Srdj, 6/12/1991"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So this is the action report submitted by the 3rd Battalion which is being forwarded by its superior command, the 9th VPS to the first administration for General Simonovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection, this is not a report drafted by the 3rd Battalion. It is a report drafted by the 9th VPS. You can see that in the letterhead and in the signature. So this is not a report drafted by the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, my point was it is exactly what -- I just repeated the title. It is "action report of the 3rd Battalion submitted by the" -- my question was being forwarded by its superior command, the 9th VPS to the first administration for General Simonovic. I read out the title as it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It does appear, Mr. Petrovic, to be an action report of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, and it appeared to be forwarded from the forward command post at Kupari.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the witness read the title. There may be a -- an ambiguity in the translation. Can the witness please read the title. This is a report about the action of the 3rd Battalion rather than a report by the 3rd Battalion. Can the witness please read the title in B/C/S, and if there are any ambiguities, I'm sure they will be dispelled after the witness reads it in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've heard the issue. You might try to clarify it with the witness then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, could you please read the title of that report.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Command of the 9th Military Naval Sector, 1300 hours on the 7th of December, 1991, forward command post Kupari, action about the operation of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade on Srdj on the 6th of December, 1991."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's dated when?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 7th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are missing a word interpretation on page 21, line 21. It says action about the operation, the word that is missing is information about the action, or report about the action. Can the witness please slowly read this line that is contestable for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, you heard the Defence counsel's concern. Could you please read the title slowly back so that it can be taken down by the stenographers.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Report about the action of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade on Srdj on the 6th of December, 1991."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And it's been forwarded by the command of the 9th VPS to the first administration for General Simonovic? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on what I see here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Would you please -- I draw your attention, Mr. Lemal, to the paragraph titled B, description of the action on Srdj 6/12/1991, and there that paragraph gives the oral tactical situation in the Srdj region is as follows. The 2nd Company of the 3rd Battalion, that is your company, in the region of Strincjera, and the topographical point is given, the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion in the region of Bosanka, the anti-armour company on Zarkovica, and the 1st Company in the region of Brgat and Dubac. That is correct, isn't it? That's what the report states?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And do you agree with those positions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the 3rd Company did not exist during that period. It had been disbanded and its personnel was attached to the 1st Company and to my company.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that the information in this document tendered by the Defence is inaccurate. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the names of the units are incorrect. As for the positions and the names of the facilities, the report is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Lemal, doesn't that paragraph indicate that in addition to the anti-armour company there were three other companies of the 3rd Battalion positioned at three different locations, which is not what you said yesterday. You said, in fact, that the battalion did not have four companies during the relevant period. So which of this is correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that during that period the battalion had the 1st Company in Bosanka village, the 2nd Company on Strincjera, Gradci, Cajkovici. I'm talking about my company here. There was an anti-armoured company which was in Zarkovica. There was a mortar company in the Uskoplje sector. There was a logistics platoon on Ivanica, and there was the battalion command in Gornji Brgat village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And this -- this paragraph, in fact, refers to the 3rd Company or a particular company being questioned at Brgat-Dubac. Is that correct or is that incorrect? Was there a company positioned at this location, Brgat-Dubac, on 6th December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Would you move on to the next page, and I don't know in the B/C/S Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. whether it follows in the same order. I'm referring you to the paragraph which starts with: "Considering that the commander of the 3rd Battalion assessed that the enemy has crossed the line of tolerance ..." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it on the same page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And do you see in that paragraph there's a reference to this effect: "He declared," referring to Captain Kovacevic, "that no one authorised that action and that he received warning on 5th December 1991 from Chief of Staff 9th VPS regarding the absolute cease-fire but that he was driven by the general action plan in the scope of which was the plan to ambush Srdj if the cease-fire was breached and when such conditions arised -- arise." Do you see that paragraph? So, Mr. Lemal, according to this document --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... speaking before you did. According to this document tendered by the Defence in evidence, contrary to what you testified, the Chief of Staff of the 9th VPS has reminded Captain Kovacevic of the cease-fire, and no one has authorised Captain Kovacevic to proceed with the attack on 6th December according to this document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. Nobody ever told me anything to that effect on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Nobody told you to what effect? Who didn't -- what are you referring to? What wasn't told to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, as a company commander, was not informed about the battalion commander that he had been informed by the Chief of Staff of the 9th VPS about the absolute cease-fire that had to be put in place. I was not informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But what -- according to what you said in evidence, were you in fact told that the attack on Srdj was authorised by Captain Kovacevic? Did he tell you anything to such effect, that he had approval to proceed with the attack on Srdj on 6th December?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was said on the 5th in the evening at the meeting which took place in Ivanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So in fact this paragraph or the contents of this document contradicts what had been told to you by Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yesterday in discussing the 3rd Company which you said was reduced to 30 men, you mentioned that commander Slovisa Sikimic was transferred. Where was he transferred and when was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was transferred after I was wounded. I don't know where he was transferred to. In any case, on my return to the battalion, I found two infantry platoons and the rest that I've told you. I don't know where he was transferred to and why.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So approximately when do you say -- what was the time frame when he was transferred? Was it in October or beginning November?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 23rd October and the 15th of November. While I was absent from my unit, he was transferred to another duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown D100.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, do you know note that under the paragraph number 1 that is titled "Written praise from the commander of the 9th VPS." Under number 15 there is a Captain Slavisa Sikimic. This is the same person you were referring to, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So on 26th November, 1991, Captain Sikimic who had been transferred in the period 23rd to 15th November is being proposed by Captain Kovacevic to be praised to obtain a written praise from the commander of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And this document, this proposal which is attached to D100, is a proposal or a recommendation being sent by Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, do you know that Captain Kovacevic lived or hails from Trebinje himself, having known him and you discussed about travelling with him in the same vehicle, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He resided in Trebinje. He had an apartment in Trebinje. As far as I know, he hails from Niksic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to move into a new area. Is this an appropriate time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Yes, we'll have the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I do beg your pardon. Previously I had indicated that I had finished the previous topic I was dealing with, but I do have to go back to it just briefly. May the witness be shown D100 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Sir, while that's being done, would you indicate as to how many men were attached to the 3rd Motorised Battalion altogether, of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, Captain Kovacevic's battalion. How many men were there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I'm unable to answer that question because I wasn't a member of the battalion command nor was I involved in that. I can just tell you how many people I had in my company.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: How many people did you have in your company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had, according to the establishment, 147 including myself, and plus that I had 16 soldiers manning mortars. So a total of 163.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So would you agree with me if I put it to you that there were approximately 600 to 700 men attached to the battalion? Is that a figure that be approximately respond -- approximately be the number, the correct number?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, do you notice that in D100, in the proposal submitted by Captain Kovacevic for commendation and promotion of soldiers and officers for their role in the normal combat activity, it lists 108 men altogether? You may not have time to count, but I have counted the number. So there are 108 officers and soldiers been proposed for commendation. Now, would you agree that this is a quite large number of persons to be recommended or proposed for commendation or promotion considering that the number of men attached to the battalion itself was 700, and the battalion was involved in the November combat operations only for three days, from 10th November to 13th November?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander may propose as many as he wishes, but I assume the command decides [as interpreted] what percentage of the manpower they will encourage and reward depending on the results achieved. Therefore, the number of men proposed doesn't mean anything. The final decision is with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I intervene in connection with the translation, please. Page 35, line 5. The witness said the superior command, not, I assume, "the command decides." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So when you said the command decides, or the superior commander decides - and in this case we are referring to the proposal made by Captain Kovacevic - were you referring to Captain Kovacevic's decision as to how many should be promoted or commended?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proposals that I made to Captain Kovacevic do not agree, coincide with this list. I suggested more men, and he made a selection of my proposals and reduced my numbers and then sent this list to his superior command and the VPS command. And most probably that command revised this list, reduced it, and finally drew up a final list of those commended and promoted. That is the practice applied. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, no. This document indicates that Captain Kovacevic has proposed 108 names. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, which doesn't mean that all the rewarded ones were also commended -- or, rather, promoted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you yourself recommended the decoration or promotion of some of the men attached to your unit. Now, since you were absent and you were not privy to the combat operations carried out in this period, how did you determine as to who should be commended or who should be promoted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday that I consulted 2nd Lieutenant Bodiroga, Nikolic Sreten, Stojanovic, and Captain Gasic who were in the unit at the time, and they presented their proposals to me which I adopted because I had no reason to doubt them as they were present and I was absent.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you consulted Lieutenant Milan Stojanovic also when arriving at this determination; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He wasn't a lieutenant, but he was one of the most prominent combatants, and he knew all those men. A lieutenant was Bodiroga, then Captain Gasic. They were the senior officers whereas Stojanovic was an ordinary soldier, a combatant.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But your testimony yesterday was that you also consulted with Milan Stojanovic in arriving at this determination. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And under -- in D100, under paragraph 9, number 10, if you would please examine the document. The paragraph titled "Medals for military accomplishment." Under IX, Milan Stojanovic is also proposed for a medal, the very same person whom you consulted in arriving at the determination as to who should be promoted or commended or rewarded.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Regarding metals for valor and promotion to higher ranks, I consulted with Captain Kovacevic. Just commendations and reward leaves for soldiers were things that I decided for my men. As for these more important rewards, I had to consult Captain Kovacevic. So I didn't make any decisions myself independently, because otherwise it would appear that I had proposed myself, and that is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You spoke about Captain Kovacevic being recommended for promotion in his role in the combat activity in November yesterday in examination-in-chief, but isn't it the case that he was in fact proposed to captain first class only after 6th December, after the 6th December incident? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When do you say he was promoted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was promoted in November.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You're certain of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He carried the rank in November. I'm certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown document P133. That's tab 41 of the Jokic binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please -- what I'm showing you, Mr. Lemal, is a document which has already been tendered in evidence before the Trial Chamber, and it is a personal file of Captain Kovacevic. Will you please turn to the page where Captain Kovacevic is being promoted to captain first class. Let me give you the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, take a few moments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It's the document -- the page bears ERN number 03390469.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you see the date there, Mr. Lemal, as 14th December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the time is counted from the 11th of November, 1991. What it says here, "Decree," that is when this promotion was covered by the document, by paperwork, because the practice in our forces is as follows: I was decorated on the 25th of November, 1991, for an action that I carried out on the 20th of March, 1991, and I received the actual document a month later.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, my question to you was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the translation there's a lot of confusion from line 6 to line 12. All the dates are confused. So could my learned friend ask the witness to explain the example he was giving more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the response is clear enough to the Prosecution. Perhaps if a further clarification is required it can be done in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation is not correct, Your Honour. I'd rather not repeat myself and indicate the errors. He didn't have any action on the 20th of March, 1991, nor any action on the 25th of November, nor did he say that. I don't know why it appeared in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, just to take you back clearly as to what you said, what you said was that you were promoted on 25th November 1991 for action carried out in October 1991. Isn't that the case? Because in the transcript it has been recorded as March 1991.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't promoted. I was decorated. I was received a medal for courage, not a rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I know. It is the date that I was --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 23rd of October was when the action was carried out, and for this I was decorated on the 25th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's right. So your decoration or you were decorated on 25th November, 1991. That would be your effective date of decoration.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, according -- according to this document, that is the personal file of Captain Kovacevic, his promotion is effective on 14 December 1991, in the same way. It is, of course, an extraordinary promotion given retroactively for his -- for the role he played in combat activity in November, but the promotion is given on 14 December 1991. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You can see with respect to all the ranks that the difference between the decree or order and the date when a rank is worn differs by a month or two. You can see when he was 2nd lieutenant and became lieutenant --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, please. Based on this record, wasn't he given a promotion on 14 December 1991 retroactively, to take effect from November 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I just told you. On the 15th of November, when I came to the unit, he was already captain first class. And that is what I'm claiming, that when I saw him then he was captain first class wearing the rank insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The promotion was given only on 14 December 1991 on record in terms the formal promotion was given only on 14 December 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was legalised on paper then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And with regard to the date 14 December 1991, wasn't it the date that General Panic visited -- visited forces of the 2nd Operational Group, including the 3rd Battalion units?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I told you yesterday that I never saw a single general or admiral in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you were commended for your combat activities in November 1991. Weren't you also -- or did you not also receive a decoration for your role in the combat activities conducted on the 6th December [Realtime transcript error read in error "November"] 1991? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I put it to you that General Panic -- I beg your pardon, Your Honour the previous question has been recorded as 6th November 1991. It should be 6th December 1991. It's page 40, line 16. I put it to you, Mr. Lemal, that on 14 December 1991, General Panic arrived with General Strugar and Admiral Jokic to visit the units of the 2nd Operational Group, especially the 3rd Battalion, which had participated in the 6th December 1991 to Zarkovica. How do you respond? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, nor was I informed about it by battalion commander, nor do I know at all that they went to the command post or to our battalion. They did not come to see me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In fact, at that time, after Captain Kovacevic had narrated to them the events of the 6th December 1991, General Strugar had ordered Captain Kovacevic to propose your name along with Lieutenant Stojanovic and Captain Nesic for decoration, which Captain Kovacevic had immediately complied with? How do you respond to it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who Misic is. That was what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Nesic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nesic. That is not correct. I received my decoration prior to that. And if such proposals were made, I have not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, yesterday when learned Defence counsel put a question to you as to whether your units participated in the combat operations of November, you went on to quite voluntarily add that in those battles the unit behaved well and they were praised by the superior command for courage. Now, what made you say that when in fact the issue put to you was as to whether your unit in fact participated in the operations? Why did you volunteer this information? Was there any particular reason why you wanted to underscore that fact?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that is what I was told by Lieutenant Sreten Nikolic who came to visit me in Bileca, in my apartment, and that is what he passed on to me, that they are doing well, that they haven't shamed me, that they're active, that they conducted themselves well and that they had been praised for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Why would he come and tell you that they hadn't shamed you in relation to the November combat operations? Is this because the Old Town was shelled in November that he found it necessary to let you know that your unit was not involved in it? Is that why? Or is it a regular statement that one would tell a commander, that the unit did not shame him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I consider it to be a normal statement by a person who is not a professional soldier but a reservist and who was proud of what he was doing. So I didn't take it to mean anything other than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your statement -- or your response infers, Mr. Lemal, that it could be considered as normal for a reservist to shame the commander. Is that what you inferred? It was -- was it a normal occurrence that perhaps a unit could in fact shame a commander and behave in such way in the course of combat activity? Did that happen often with regard to 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never thought about it, and it has nothing to do with this. I consider it to be quite normal and natural for someone to say that if he took part in combat operations and there were no casualties and no material losses, it is quite normal for any commander to be proud of that, to be proud of having managed to carry out an operation without suffering any wounded or dead or without losing any equipment. I consider that to be quite normal, at least in an army.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Lieutenant Nikolic also informed you that the Old Town had been shelled by perhaps other units of the 3rd Battalion and not your unit during the course of the combat operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand about which period of time we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm referring to the combat operations conducted by the 3rd Battalion from 10th November to 13th November. Did Lieutenant Nikolic inform you that the Old Town had been shelled during this period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did he learn afterwards that the Old Town had been shelled during this period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you about the 6th, and I saw it, but as for the other, no one informed me about it, nor did I learn about it from anyone else later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
