utterances.text: Did you see media reports or news reports that foreign observers were visiting, journalists were visiting Dubrovnik and the Old Town because it had been shelled in the period 10th November to 13th November? Are you saying that you had not up to date heard of this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear that from the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you do know that the Old Town was shelled during these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I heard from the media, just like anybody else. Now, whether I know about it personally, I said I saw it on television. I was at home in Belica. I heard about the arrival of the European Community monitors and observers and that they went to the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, you testified yesterday in examination-in-chief that the November operations -- that in the November operations Donji Brgat, Bosanka, Zarkovica, Kula Grac [sic], and Kula Strincjera were captured; is that correct? That's what you said in your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that? I think you made a mistake in one of the names of the places?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I probably mispronounced and I beg your pardon for that. Donji Brgat, Bosanka, Zarkovica, Kula Graci, and Kula Strincjera were captured in November operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Gornji Brgat, not Donji Brgat. That's the correction. And as to the others, not captured but taken control of. So if that's the case my answer is yes. Gornji Brgat, the village of Bosanka, Zarkovica, Kula Strincjera, Kula Graci, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, since you were not there, did you learn this also from Lieutenant Nikolic? Whereas he the one who told you as to what had transpired during the course of the November operations as to what territory was captured?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until his arrival in the unit, mostly him and afterwards the others, the fellow fighters who were in the unit, fellow combatants, would inform me about our unit, where it went and how it fared.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, having captured Zarkovica, the observation post of the battalion was established on Zarkovica. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the observation post.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And once Brgat was captured, the 3rd Battalion command was established in Brgat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what you say is that these areas, especially Zarkovica and Gornji Brgat, were captured in November. The combat operations carried out between 10th November and 13th November. That's your position or that's how you were informed.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was captured a little earlier on. Gornji Brgat was captured earlier on, because it was a pass that was taken control of. I don't know, according to what they said, that was all earlier on, 7th, 8th. 6th, 7th, or 8th. I can't be specific, I don't know, on the basis of what they told me when Gornji Brgat was captured. And later on it went further on towards Zarkovica and the village of Bosanka and all the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So even if you take as 6th, it was in the November operations that these two places, Zarkovica and Brgat, were captured. That's your position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's what it was, around the 6th, and that Brgat was previously captured and then they moved on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Isn't it the case that Zarkovica and Brgat were captured -- had been captured by 25th October 1991? That is, October -- in the course of the October combat operations and not November operation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, yes. I don't know exactly. As I say, I did not take part myself. But I do know that it was during this period of time, that is to say, from the 23rd of October when I left until I returned, that the places you mentioned were captured. That's true. Now, as to the dates of the actual capture when, these places were captured, I'm not quite sure, and I wouldn't venture or hazard a guess.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, there was only one major combat operation carried out by units of the 3rd Battalion together with other units of the 2nd Operational Group in October, isn't it? That was in the period 23rd, 24th, 25th October; is that correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: I left on the 23rd. I left and went to hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In November there was only one combat operation carried out by the 3rd Battalion, which was in the period 8th November to 13th November. Isn't that correct? I beg your pardon. 3rd Battalion was not involved. Let me rephrase. In the period 8th of November to 13th November, forces of the 2nd Operational Group carried out one combat operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably that was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And your testimony so far before this Trial Chamber was that Zarkovica and Brgat were captured in the November combat operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave you the period which I'm sure of, and that's the one from the 23rd of October, when I was wounded, up until the 15th. It is during that period of time that those places, those features and villages were captured, and that is as precise as I can be. Anything else would be guesswork.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Is now you're saying between the period 23rd October to November, once I put it to you that these two places were captured in fact on the 25th October, but previously what you said was in the period 6th November onwards; isn't that correct? You're including the date the 23rd October once I put it to you that it was captured on 25th October?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I say again, I don't know if it was captured exactly on the 25th. I really can't say. I couldn't give you an exact date. The period from till -- from the 23rd to the 15th of November. I was not in the unit during that period of time, and that's when those features were captured. That is true. Now, whether there was one operation or two operations, whether it was done all in one go or not, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So in fact what you're saying is that you really cannot say since when the battalion observation post was established at Zarkovica or since when the battalion command was established at Brgat. You cannot say with certainty.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that it was there 100 per cent from the 15th of November when I arrived. Now, when it was first established, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: How many 82-millimetre mortar pieces did the entire 3rd Battalion have in all of its units? Would you be able to give an approximate figure?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I myself had four.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And obviously you would be aware that the battalion had other 82-millimetre mortars apart from your four pieces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I should know. Probably I should know, but I don't know about the others. I know about myself for sure and for the establishment units. Now, whether there was anything else anywhere else, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you don't know about what the other companies had or how many other 82-millimetre mortars the battalion had? You cannot say?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. I can only speak for myself. I know how many I had, and those are the figures that I can give you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you -- did you have a direct line of site to the Libertas Hotel and Iva Vojnovica Street from your position at Strincjera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And do you know if there was such a direct line of sight to those two places from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure. I was at Zarkovica just once or twice perhaps throughout that time. I won't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So that's how you said you could see that vehicle called Charlie when it goes about on Iva Vojnovica Street? You had a clear line of site to that street?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very clearly. You can see the whole street very clearly and the whole area round about from the Strincjera fort.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now you stayed and observed that vehicle Charlie firing from close to the stadium at an adjacent unit. I think you mentioned the place as Osojnik. Osojnik. Pardon my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that was before the 6th of December, not for that day. It was before that they fired from there. And I conveyed this to my commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I did not ask you about 6th, Mr. Lemal. Did you have a direct line of sight from Strincjera to this stadium?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when did you see this particular vehicle firing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think it was the end of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And did you see the vehicle travel down Iva Vojnovica Street up to the stadium before firing or was it stationed by the stadium at the time when you first saw the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It fired from the crossroads at the stadium. We saw that point in time when that happened, and it went off in the direction of the Libertas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And did you -- before it fired, did you see it coming to that position from somewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: How long did you observe this vehicle firing and then leaving? About how long did it take for all that to take place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it fired two shells from there and then went off, and we followed him until he went round the corner in a little forested area by the Libertas Hotel, and that would be about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So during that ten minute -- ten minutes, what was the difficulty for you to fire one of your own weapons at this vehicle and destroy it? Why did you just stand around and watch that vehicle firing for all that ten minutes? Is that the kind of logical conduct one could expect in the context of the situation prevalent around Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it would have fired had the people -- my people been up at the mortar positions. There was a cease-fire on at that moment, and I didn't keep my men by the artillery pieces, but they were further away at Kula. Had it -- they been nearer, probably we would have fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you just stood around at your position in clear view of the vehicle Charlie, because if you had direct line of sight to the vehicle, they would see you, too, and watched this whole process for ten minutes while the vehicle fired?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: My Strincjera Kula, or tower, can be seen every day from Dubrovnik, and all movement on the part of my men outside the walls can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You said that you observed Croat firing positions in Velika Petka. Now, that is the hill to the east of Mala Petka, very close to it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In fact, if you look at -- look towards Mala Petka from Strincjera, it is the hill just in front of Mala Petka; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be, but if you provide me with a map, if we're talking about locations like that and geographical positions, I could perhaps take a look at it and tell you for certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's all right, Mr. Lemal, I'll move on. Now, the location that you referred to as Ispod Petka Lapad is very close to Iva Vojnovica Street, isn't it correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when we talk about toponyms, the witness asked for the map. So if my learned colleague is going to continue along this line of questioning and refer to places, could he be provided with a map, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary, Mr. Petrovic. He gave sufficient indication of acceptance of the proposition put to him without the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So your previous response to the question has not gone down, that is that the location referred to as Ispod Petka Lapad is very close to Iva Vojnovica Street and you nodded but that does not get taken down. Could you respond with a yes or no without nodding because the transcript Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. has to take down your response.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's where the street ends, Vojnovica street ends and after that it's the Lenjin Bulevar. I think that's how it is

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Iva Vojnovica street becomes Lenjin Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So it's a yes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now the place you indicated as Kotorska Ulica is just north to Libertas Hotel, very near to it, isn't it? In fact you did say that it was close to Libertas Hotel yesterday. But to the north [Realtime transcript read in error "not north"], very close to the Libertas Hotel, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, were you close to Captain Kovacevic and did you have the opportunity to have conversations with him often? You said in fact that you took lifts in his vehicle to Kupari yesterday.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Your Honour. There is a misprint in the transcript. I said it was close to Libertas Hotel yesterday and it has gone down as not north, but it should be to the north. Not north but to the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, that certainly was what you were putting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you also said that Captain Kovacevic reported to the forward command post in Kupari and that you knew this because you travelled with him to Kupari and that perhaps he told you about it. How did you know that he was reporting to the forward command post in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time in Kupari, to provide security for the command post, there was my school friend, Sijeric Niko, who was a lieutenant. And he was later transferred to Mokosica, and until he went to Mokosica on about two occasions I went with Captain Kovacevic to Kupari to visit him so that we could see each other because we hadn't seen each other for two or three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what -- what is the time frame in which Captain Kovacevic reported to Kupari or when you got to know that he was reporting to Kupari? Can you indicate approximately what the time frame was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period from the 15th of November until the 6th of December, in that time frame. That's when I went down there with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So even the week between 15th to 20th he was reporting to Kupari. That's your position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Would you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did he report to -- now, you gave the period between 15th November to 6th December. Do you know if he reported to Kupari between the period 15th November to 20th November?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know. Possibly during that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you remember going down with him to Kupari during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave you the period of time for which I can guarantee. All the rest would be impossible to say specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know to which command the 3rd Battalion reported in October?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 472nd Brigade in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And so as far as you know, the reporting to Kupari was only after 15th November?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know up until 20 -- 20th of November the 3rd Battalion was within the 472nd Motorised Brigade and therefore it would have to report to the brigade command during the period 15th November to 20th November? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown P101. That's tab 3 of the Jokic binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This -- I appreciate that you may not have seen this document before, Mr. Lemal. It's in evidence before the Trial Chamber. Do you see from this document that on 20th November an order has been issued for the 472nd Motorised Brigade leaving the 3rd Battalion under the subordination of the 9th VPS to move out of the 9th VPS and to report directly to the -- 2nd OG Command and be attached to the 2nd Corps? Do you see that from this document? Isn't that what this document says?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So isn't it clear then -- then that the 3rd Battalion could have reported directly to the 9th VPS only after this date, 20th November?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So is it then clear to you, Mr. Lemal, that you have not had proper information or sufficient information about whom your battalion commander was report -- reporting to or the relevant dates or time frames? Is that clear to you now? Would you agree that that is the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just saying what I knew about, what I knew happened. I didn't consider it necessary for me to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have finished cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Mahindaratne. Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lemal, I kindly ask you to tell us, the call that took place on the 5th of December, 1991, by which you were invited to go to the command post of Captain Jeremic in Ivanica, who was it who called you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was called by the duty officer in the Gornji Brgat command post of the battalion commander, Captain Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If I understand you well, the call was communicated to you by the duty officer at the command post in Gornji Brgat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Battalion, Vladimir Kovacevic, at the moment when you were called to come for briefing, was he at the command post in Gornji Brgat?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not at the command post because it was emphasised to me not to come to the command post but to go to the command post of Captain Jeremic in Ivanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Captain Kovacevic, commander of your battalion, immediately after you -- very soon after you, did he arrive in Ivanica in -- at the command post of Captain Zlatan Jeremic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown the map P132. Can the map be placed on the ELMO to show Kupari, Dubrovnik, and that general area. Can you put it up a bit. Thank you. Can this be zoomed in a little, please. Thank you. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, can you use your pointer and show us where you were when you received the call from Gornji Brgat to come for this meeting? Can you please show us where you were? What is the name of this place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cajkovici village is the name of this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is that place on the positions where your troops were deployed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please show us where Gornji Brgat is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you also show us Dubac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And also Kupari, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The road from Kupari towards Ivanica, the place where the meeting took place, can you show the road, the way it leads from Kupari to Ivanica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please name the places on the road from Kupari to Ivanica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kupari, Dubac, then you go up to Gornji Brgat, and from there to Ivanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you described and said that you saw only one vehicle negotiated -- negotiating the road uphill, the only vehicle that was behind you, can you please show on the map where you were and where that vehicle was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the crossroads in Gornji Brgat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there's a road forking off towards Ivanica, and I saw the vehicle here in the direction of Dubac driving from Kupari towards the Dubac crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Ivanica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Gornji Brgat to Ivanica, this vehicle was some five minutes behind me and arrived in Ivanica some five minutes after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Who got out of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Captain Kovacevic, the battalion commander who got out of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were asked by my learned friend about the times when things happened on the 6th of December when you started moving towards Srdj, when you arrived at Srdj, the times when some of your men were killed, how long was the fire going on for, and the time when you withdrew, today, 13 years after the events, can you be very specific in determining the exact times of the events that took place on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only time that I'm absolutely sure about is that I left fort Strincjera at 05. The artillery support started at 6.00. All the other times I'm not sure about because I was in combat. I didn't have a wristwatch that I could consult in order to check the times.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your participation in combat on Srdj, how many contacts did you have with battalion commander over the radio?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had two contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In any of these contacts did you mention a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The cease-fire was not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: During the cross-examination, you were asked about the reporting and the meeting in the battalion headquarters after the 6th of December when you were talking about the operation on Srdj, and you said that the commander had criticised Captain Nesic with regard to Stari Grad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did Captain Nesic respond in any way to the commander's criticism with regard to Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did respond. He said that whenever he launched a shell it was because he had noticed fire being opened from those places towards Bosanka and repeater station on Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where was it that he noticed the fire coming from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He mentioned a fort or a fortress whose name I don't know. He mentioned Stradun. He mentioned the open market and some other places which I can't remember at the moment. They were all in the Old Town, and from those places fire was being opened. He also mentioned a small harbour whose name I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Old City harbour?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the one that you can see from Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in responding to the battalion commander's criticism Captain Nesic mentioned the fire points in the Old Town from which fire was opened towards Bosanka and the other forts or the point that you mentioned which I can't remember?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The repeater station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wanted to point out that counsel was leading the witness but it's a little too late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did Captain Nesic say or mention who was it who was opening fire or from what weapons or arms?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did mention the pieces of artillery and weapons starting with sniper, the anti-aircraft gun, to mortars, and he also drew these points on a map for the commander. I wasn't really interested in the deployment of those fire points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour, because in cross-examination this witness clearly said he couldn't quite remember exactly what the criticism was, and his testimony was in fact that he remembers some form of criticism levelled against Captain Nesic by Captain Kovacevic, and now you have details of this criticism coming out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's not really a point of objection, Ms. Mahindaratne, but a point that goes very much to the weight to be attached to the evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, in response to my learned friend's questions, you said that the death of your two soldiers who were killed on Srdj was due to the artillery which failed to open fire from Cilipi; is that correct? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any other fallen soldiers during the operation on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mesaros from the 1st Company belonging to Captain Stojanovic was also killed, and this was also directly caused by the artillery failing to open fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many soldiers were killed during that operation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: A total of five.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many were wounded?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I'd say a dozen or so were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you blame the artillery from Cilipi for all these deaths and injuries?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. The witness is being asked to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, I think not, Ms. Mahindaratne. The question is what was this witness's view or opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, save for the death of one of my soldiers during the advance, all the other deaths and all the other injuries are a direct consequence of the fact that the artillery failed to open fire on the target which were beyond our reach. I'm referring to the artillery in Cilipi. And this is what I said to my commander during the debriefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What are those targets that were beyond your range?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the mortar targets or firing points on Petka, on Babin Kuk, and in the tennis grounds sector on Petka. All of these were beyond our range.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does that mean -- or in respect of those firing points, the only efficient fire could only come from Cilipi and neutralise those firing points.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very clear from the position of -- of our fire support they could not reach those targets, and the only ones that could open fire successfully on all of those points is the artillery in Cilipi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 5th of December, were you promised there would be artillery support from Cilipi during the operation on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was promised. Both the artillery from Cilipi and the artillery from Osojnik were supposed to support us. However, the artillery from Osojnik could not open fire on those targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown D65.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, on your cross-examination were you shown this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I read parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Who is the author of this document? Who is it who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 9th Naval Military Sector in its forward command post in Kupari. And this is a report about the action of the 3rd Battalion during the operation on Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Under the first two items, can you see the information about the officers who are indicated here? Who are those officers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And who else?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Miroslav Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the end of the description. What does it say about each of them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Extremely skilled and brave officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does it also say about Lieutenant Jovanovic and Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It does say that about both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Whose opinion is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the opinion of the commander of the 9 Military Sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour. I don't think the witness is in a position to respond to that as to whose opinion it is. 16

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for the interruption. If I may, I'd like to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has before him a document that was the subject of cross-examination. He was asked to interpret the document or say what he knows about the document, and my question was exactly to that same effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're asking particularly who held a certain opinion, and there seems to be some disputation as to who was the particular author. The witness's answer can go no further than to say, well, it's in a document that is under the authority, apparently, of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document was signed by the commander, and it is a document of the command of the 9th VPS. As my learned friend, during the cross-examination, tried to give the impression that the document was compiled as a report of the 3rd Battalion, I believe that certain things mentioned in this document speak to the opposite regarding the characteristics that I referred to in my question, indicate who is compiling the document and who is giving those opinions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point of your question and the effect of the answer, I think, have been sufficiently identified, Mr. Rodic. This is a document which we know from evidence was drafted by others, was signed by the commander. Now, when you are asking whose opinion was that, you have the problem that the authorship was somebody other than the person who eventually signed. As I've put it to you, the document can be accepted because of the signature as being a document which expressed views which had the apparent authority of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand that perfectly, but I'm afraid that your comments and your opinion were already stated once linked to the document dated the 9th of December. That is the report of the commission on damage done to the Old Town. As for this document, I really do not remember that it was ever stated that it had been written by any other than the author indicated for this command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, I can only do my best when an issue like this arises to recall evidence that stretches back over some months. When we come to finally assess the evidence, not only myself but all members of the Chamber, have to go over that evidence and be sure that we have it accurately recalled. At the moment, to ask this witness whose opinion appears in a document, you can go really no more than the fact that there is an apparent signature and that is the person who has -- either the original source of the opinion or somebody who is prepared to put a signature to a document in which that opinion has been expressed by somebody else. Now, isn't that enough for your purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, tell me, please, in that document that you have in front of you, is there any mention of a mortar company led by Captain Jeremic at Ivanica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In what context?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he had started preparations for the attack, firing exclusively at Srdj using 120-millimetre mortars at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need that document any longer. So could the witness now be shown Exhibit D100, Defence Exhibit D100.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, this is a document you are familiar with. Tell me, what is the date on which it was compiled.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of September, 1991 -- I'm sorry, the 26th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: These are proposals for incentives; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When are incentives granted or for what purpose are they given or proposed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: For results achieved in carrying out assignments on the part of individuals or units as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: For what period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the past period in relation to the date when the proposals are made.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need that document any longer either. You mentioned that briefings in your battalion were held at the command post at Brgat, sometimes at Ivanica, and sometimes the battalion commander would go from one company to another and be reported to orally from company commanders personally; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What form of briefing was more frequent, individual or at a meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was more frequent at a meeting at the command post which we would all attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At those briefings, would the commander mention any individual officer outside your battalion with respect to the assignments given to your battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was frequent mention of somebody coming from a superior command. So he would say to me, for instance, "Lemal, take care. Zec is coming on an inspection, or Nesic. Vlado Kovacevic will be coming tomorrow to check things out." So he would mention the names of the senior others. Or when Sofronije would come with the Spanish officer, then a day earlier it would be announced, and it was in that context that senior officers outside our battalion were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And where were those officers from? What command did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: They belonged to the 9th VPS, and they were accommodated in Kupari.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, just one more question. During the examination-in-chief, I asked you about photographs. You had some photographs from that period of time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I still have those photographs. They are in my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is shown on those photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. I did not question the witness at all with regard to these photographs that were raised in the course of examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct, Your Honour. I quite agree with the objection. I just want to complete my re-examination with the question whether the witness would state to Your Honours once again whether he's willing to provide the Chamber with those photographs and to explain when they were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you can leave that. The matter has not been taken up. So that concludes your re-examination, does it, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Lemal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I just ask, we didn't get your present rank at any stage. Could you indicate your present rank.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My present rank is major for another ten days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What happens then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I will acquire the rank of lieutenant colonel. That is the plan at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm -- I'm happy to say that that concludes your evidence here. Thank you very much for your assistance, and you may of course now return to your duties. Could I indicate to counsel that the time taken with Major Lemal was well in excess of estimates, and we would certainly be at great risk of completing our evidence within the time available if that sort of time is spent with all the witnesses to come. So will counsel keep that in mind. I think this is a convenient time now for the second break. Could I indicate that we will resume at a quarter to. If people could be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please take the card and read the affirmation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You could sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. For the record, will you tell us your first and last name, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Vlado Pepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The 24th of February, 1959, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, tell us, please, what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I'm an officer in the army of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is your present rank, please?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I am a frigate captain at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what rank does that rank correspond to in the ground forces.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It corresponds to the rank of lieutenant colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, would you please tell us what is your educational background.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the naval academy. That lasts four years. And before that, of course eight years of elementary school and four years of grammar school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you completed the naval academy. Can you tell us what is your speciality?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I graduated in the naval section, and my speciality was artillery rocket speciality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where was the naval military academy situated in?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: In Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you served upon graduation from the naval academy?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I graduated in 1982. From 1982 until 1985, I served in Split. From 1985 up to the present, I have been serving in Kumbor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, from 1985 until 1992 - let us take that period of time - in that period which unit were you serving in?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: In the 9th Military Naval Sector, in the 107th artillery mobile artillery battery of 130-millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown document 46, and could it be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, that D or P46?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, while we're looking for the document, could you tell us what is the abbreviation for this unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: 107th OAG, Coastal Artillery Group, OAG. G as Gacko -- as in Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the table that you have in front of you. It is a structure of the units of the 9th VPS. And show us, please, if you see on this table the unit you served in. Would you point to it, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness is pointing to the 107th OAG within the 9th VPS. Thank you. We don't need the document any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, you told us that you were part of the 9th VPS, that is the 107th OAG. Tell us, please, whether you were in that status also in October, November, and December 1991, that is, a member of the 107th OAG belonging to the VPS. Will you tell us, please, a little about the composition of the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The 107th OAG, to make things quite clear, was designed to defend the coastal belt roughly from Dubrovnik to Bar. It consisted of active and reserve artillery batteries. It had five batteries, one of which was live, live meaning that it was manned by active duty personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In October 1991, the 107th OAG consisted of how many batteries and what weapons were they provided with?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: In October 1991, the 107th OAG had two live batteries of 85 millimetres, which was taken from the reserve, and my own of 130-millimetre calibre. The section manning cannon was active, whereas the defensive section or battery consisted of reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In which of these two batteries were you serving in?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the 130-millimetre calibre battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us in a sentence what kind of a weapon a 130-millimetre cannon is. Very, very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It is an extremely effective and highly precise weapon, with very high precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How many 130-millimetre cannon were there in your battery?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: At that point in time there were four guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you told us you were the commander of the 130-millimetre calibre battery. Who was the commander of the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was Lieutenant Colonel Vinko Stamenov. Stamenov, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, would you please tell us with respect to October 1991, again very briefly, where was your battery located or, rather, the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: In October there were two locations. At the beginning of October -- or, rather, three locations. At the beginning of October, we were advancing. The first position was in the village of Karasovici close to Grude. After that we were at the Grude football stadium of the Slavan [phoen] football club, and towards the end of the month we were at Cilipi airport between two runways.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When was the 130-millimetre battery deployed to Cilipi airport?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: At the very end of October and up until the 4th of November, 1991. The digging in took that amount of time. So the ground in between two runways was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how long that 130-millimetre battery was located at the airport in Cilipi?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Up until the 19th of May, 1992. Correction, please. I don't remember with certainty. It was the beginning of 1992 where we were transferred from the Cilipi airport to the village of Popovici, which was quite close to Cilipi, and that is where we stayed until the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was the command post of the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: In October you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the time you were at Cilipi airport where was the command post of the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: In the airport building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, that means from the beginning of November onwards, your 107th OAG was at the positions we mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was there in November and December 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about an observation post? Did that exist for targeting the firepower of the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where was that observation post during the material time, November/December 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: At Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In November, for instance, 1991, did your unit take part in any combat operations?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly to the best of your recollections what kind of combat operations they were?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was during the liberation of the village or, rather, taking control of the village of Bosanka, and that began on the 8th of November, and my unit was operational along the Lokrum -- the island of Lokrum.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And where were you yourself during those combat operations of the 8th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: As the commander, I was at the observation post in the target area, and I directed the fire, the targeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you say "observation post," which one do you mean?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The Zarkovica one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long did you take part in those operations, the operations of your battery in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Until the afternoon of the 9th when I was wounded and when I went to hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, when were you wounded and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I was wounded in the afternoon. Around 2.00 or 3.00 in the afternoon of the 9th of May [as interpreted], and I was wounded because throughout that entire day we were being fired at from the region of Strincjera, mortar fire and shells. And one of those shells I wasn't able to take cover on time and I was wounded in the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For the purposes of the record, tell us what date that was.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The 9th of November, at around 1400 hours or 1500 hours, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us where you were wounded and do you have any scars from that wound today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For the purposes of the record, 73, 2 I think wrongly records 9th of May. It should be 9th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, of course, and I repeated the question twice in the hope of it being corrected but I'm going to have to do it a third time I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So tell us the day, the date that you were wounded.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was Mitrovdan, the 9th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, let the record reflect that the witness indicated his wound on the head with his finger, the place he was wounded. It was on the forehead on the left. Your Honour, I have a document here now which I'd like to ask the witness to look at very briefly, two documents in fact. The documents have not been translated since the witness brought them in with him when he arrived, and they just refer to his wounding and that is the sole purpose that we're going to use the documents for and will be presented. They will of course be translated as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, would you please take a look at these two documents and tell us what they are.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of November, I was transported or, rather, I went -- I was still able to move, so I went to the Meljine hospital, and I was attended to there. My head was X-rayed. It was bleeding profusely. As the hospital did not have the facilities to extract the shrapnel from my head, I was transported to the neurosurgical department of the Lisan [phoen] hospital which is where one shrapnel were extracted. The others were smaller and were not extracted because they were not deemed to be dangerous. So this is a discharge letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this first document dated the 12th of November, 1992, could you read the date out, please, and the title of the document, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It says specialist hospital for orthopaedics, neurosurgery, neurology, medical rehabilitation Lasa Cukic [phoen], the 12th of November, 1991. It is a discharge letter with the epicrisis. And epicrisis is of course the Latin term that they use.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document as a Defence exhibit, the document dated the 12th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D101.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the second document, please, and just read out the title, what it says in the heading.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It is a letter for specialist examination addressed to the medical sanitary or medical corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: So this is a letter of referral.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now read what page 2 says.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It says: "Sick leave until the 2nd of December, 1991." And afterwards: "Treatment completed, patient healthy."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to tender this document as well as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D102. Excuse me, D -- yes, D102.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, from what direction did the party open fire which led to your wounding?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It occurred the previous day, as soon as the attack on Bosanka was launched. So they started firing at the observation post. And since the observation post was from where they directed their operation, I was not able to observe where this was coming from, where the shooting -- firing was coming from. I assumed that it was to my right, which means from where the fort of Strincjera lies roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell us, please, whose forces were they that were there and who fired at you, the firing that led to your wounding?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: There were the paramilitary formations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The witness just said in the previous answer he didn't know where the fire was coming from. Now the new question is, "What forces were firing -- what forces were firing upon you?" If he doesn't know where the firing is coming from and he's only speculating, he can't say who was firing upon him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You better try and pin that down, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I thought it said in the B/C/S -- I thought the answer in the B/C/S allowed my question, but I assume it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said you were wounded, Mr. Pepic, and that you were wounded at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What wounded you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: May I be allowed to complete my previous answer? I didn't know at the time, but afterwards when I returned to my unit, my officer told me where I was wounded from and the weapon used. So I know exactly which artillery piece was used and what wounded me, because as soon as I was transported to hospital a mortar was found there and that mortar was neutralised, put out of action. And a mortar was found, an 82-millimetre one, and it was that weapon that wounded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And to whom did that artillery piece belong to?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: As I said, it belonged to the paramilitary formations which had taken control between Strincjera and the north-west of them, several hundred metres to the north-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you say paramilitaries, whose paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, the HVO I think they were called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The HVO. Which side did they belong to? What side was that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, how shall I put it? How can I explain this? At that time in my unit, I had recruits from --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please limit your answers to my questions. If you can tell us, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, how long you were absent for.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Until the 2nd of December of that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And where were you until the 2nd of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I was in hospital for seven days, I think, in Resanje [phoen] and in Meljine, and after that I underwent treatment at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So when did you return to your unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: On the 2nd of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what duty did you take up?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: My own. Battery commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who was the commander at that time of the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The same, Lieutenant Colonel Stamenov.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about the 5th of December, 1991? Were you in your unit then too?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 5th of December did you receive an order of any kind?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who did you receive an order from?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: From my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name and surname of your commander?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Vinko Stamenov.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what order did Stamenov issue to you on that 5th of December?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The order was that by 6.00 a.m. I should go to the observation post and lend fire support to the battalion in taking control of the Srdj feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what day did the order refer to?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When, roughly speaking, what time of day did Stamenov give you this order?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Towards evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he say how you were to open fire on that day, the 6th of December, what your -- what manner your operations should take?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I was resubordinated to the battalion commander, that is to say Captain Kovacevic, and he indicated the targets that I was to fire at.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when did -- no. I withdraw that question. In the answer to the previous question, you said that you were ordered to go to the observation post?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, which observation post and why was it necessary to have your presence at that observation post?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: To Zarkovica, and my presence was needed for the planned operation and targeting the fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The observation post concerned of your battery at Zarkovica, was it constantly manned by members of your battery?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. It was manned only when we expected an attack or when we planned an operation of our own. Otherwise, there were fewer men. An expected attack, an attack launched against us I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the 2nd to, let's say, the 5th of December at the observation post of your battery, were there members of your unit manning it there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you, on the next day, start carrying out the orders you had received from your unit commander?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you actually did?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I took a vehicle and a soldier, a radio operator, I took the radio device and started out for the observation post using the Cilipi, Brgat, Zarkovica road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what did you do when you reached Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I manned the observation point, checked the radio communications lines and reported to the command or headquarters and Captain Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What state was your battery in on that morning of the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was on the alert, in a state of readiness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you mean by state of momentary readiness?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It means we were ready to open fire at any given moment. Once I had given the command, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, when you reached Zarkovica, did you notice any firing in the area you were in at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what you saw, what you noticed.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: There was artillery preparation -- there was preparation -- undergoing preparation for any artillery attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see what the targets that were being fired at were when you arrived at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Srdj feature was being fired at.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who -- or, rather, did you see -- or who did you see at the Zarkovica plateau, which is where you were at that time at around 6.00?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The commander of the anti-armoured company, Nesic. Then there was the commander Vlado Kovacevic. And I'm not quite sure when I noticed this first, but there was warship captain Milan Zec as well. But he came after I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When, approximately did Captain Zec arrive, and how long did he stay in the Zarkovica plateau?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The first time I noticed him was after 8.00, and he was there during the entire operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time were you requested to open fire?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: At 0800, Captain Nesic pointed the position of the mortar -- mortars on the tennis ground by the Libertas Hotel. He did it through binoculars. They were opening fire on Mount Srdj. At that moment our forces were already on Mount Srdj. And from the sector of Libertas Hotel and the aforementioned mortars, fire was opened on our forces on Mount Srdj. At that moment, Captain Nesic, that is Captain Kovacevic, asked me to open fire on that target because I was the only one in whose range those targets were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you open fire on those targets?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did order the beginning of fire. However, the response was that the fire was not approved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who did you issue this order to, to open fire?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I -- I issued that to my officer and to my firing line. However, the response that the fire was not approved was returned through the same radio communication by Branimir Lukic, the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the course of that day, were you again requested to open fire?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was requested on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who requested that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was always Captain Kovacevic, because I noticed clearly one mortar. The other one was hidden from me because they were both on the border of the wood and the edge of the tennis grounds. Since they could open fire on Srdj, there had been losses already by then. I remember that soldier Mesoras Tasod [phoen] had been killed. It was requested from me to neutralise these two pieces of weapon -- weapons because Captain Kovacevic did not have any other weapons in whose range those two mortars would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, during that morning, have any communication, the technical communication with your firing positions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Absolutely I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Captain Kovacevic have direct link with his superior command during that morning?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Captain Kovacevic at one point complain about the possible problems that he might have had with his superior command?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which was Kovacevic's superior command, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was your superior command, the superior command to the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you saw Captain Nesic on Zarkovica plateau. Can you tell us who Captain Nesic is?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Captain Nesic was the commander of the anti-armour company of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What equipment did he have at his disposal --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: He had --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Allow me to put my question and then you can start answering it. What equipment did he have at his disposal?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: He had the classical anti-armour pieces, Maljutkas, the recoilless gun 82-millimetre, and he also had a 60-millimetre mortar as part of his weaponry. And I believe that he also had a 76-millimetre ZIS weapons, but I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please ask the witness to draw on a piece of paper the situation as it was on Zarkovica, depicting the place where he was, also the place where Captain Nesic's pieces were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And if you can, just do a rough sketch.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Started using the Cyrillic script here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You don't have to give us any details, just basic things. Could you please put your sketch on the ELMO. Can you please point to us the place where you were.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: This is where I was together with Nesic. This is where Nesic's units -- unit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please here where you were. Could you please put number 1 next to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Slow down. The interpreters are having a great battle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, we have to be careful and make a pause between my question and your answer. Can you please listen to my question and then answer now, and I will also slow down. Can you put a cross next to the place where you were and also mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What else can we see in this sketch?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: This is where my observation post was. Captain Nesic was also here. This is where I noticed one recoilless gun, an 82-millimetre gun. And here below me, this is a pine tree. And below that was a 9K 11 Lancer. The so-called Maljutka. This is the direction Dubrovnik, the direction Bosanka, that is Srdj as we go further, and this is Brgat, and this is the direction Cilipi or the in other words the place where my unit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where the recoilless gun was, place number 2 next to it.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The BSD stands for recoilless gun; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you now mark the place where the Maljutka was, putting number 3 next to it.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where was the command post of Captain Nesic? Was it in the same place that is marked by number 1?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you put number 4 next to Commander Nesic's commander -- command post.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where was Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Captain Kovacevic was always in the sector behind us. He would move around here. From Zarkovica he was leading the whole operation, and he moved from one place to another in order to have a better view of the advance of his two units towards Srdj on the slopes towards the peak where new forces were expected to be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the sector through which Captain Kovacevic moved as far as you can remember.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please put number 5 next to this line.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is the surface of this Zarkovica plateau? How big is this area?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Maybe 50 by 50. It is at the peak of an observation point, and as you can see here, it was surrounded by walls. It was a hunting facility with some fixed facilities. One was here. The other was here. The third was here, and one was behind my back, not on the very peak itself. It is a peak with a very good view but lower than Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please indicate all these facilities that were there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What could be found in these buildings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Nothing. They were empty. These two here did not have roofs. This here had already been hit by a mortar shell when I was injured, and this here was also damaged because a lot of mortar shells fell in front of it. They were all damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And now tell -- tell us your communication means. Where was your radio set?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was at my command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where was the radio set of Captain Nesic or Captain Kovacevic, depending on the situation?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: They had mobile communication means, and I don't know. I'm not sure where those were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D103.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, let's go back to the 5th December, Mr. Pepic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you had received an order from the commander of the 107th OAG, Vinko Stamenov.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can we please clarify this? How did this order get to be issued? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Are you say -- are you trying -- are you asking me to say who ordered that to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was the command of the 9th VPS, his superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Colonel Stamenov go for some briefings?
