utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Every day regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did these briefings took place?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: At the forward command post in Kupari.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What command was there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was the forward command post Kupari of the 9th VPS, the 9th Military Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 5th of December, did he go for a briefing at the forward command post in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he convey this order to you on his return?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the briefing -- let's us just clarify one thing. Did Colonel Stamenov convey this order to you from his return from the briefing that took place in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At page 86, 17, I think the date 5 December 1991 has been omitted from your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I did say that, but I can see that it hasn't been recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the 6th December. You have told us that on several occasions you were requested to open fire. On that day did your unit open fire at all?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, was fire opened from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you observe from Zarkovica the fire points -- some of the fire points on that day on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What firing points did you yourself observe from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: As I've already told you, Captain Nesic pointed me through his sights. The mortar point by the Lokrum hotel on the border of the tennis courts. Even without those sighting equipment I could notice an anti-aircraft gun at the entrance to the Old Town by the old harbour, and I also observed an 82-millimetre mortar. I also observed the fire being opened from a mortar in one of the side streets next to Stradun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let -- let us draw a line between the Old Town and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've been given specific discovery as to what this witness would say. We've been given an initial note, a second note, and information by telephone calls, and this information is outside the information provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on several occasions I have informed my learned friend by telephone as to what the contents of this testimony would be in addition to two written documents that I have provided him with. That was yesterday afternoon around 5.00 or 6.00, and I told him that as a result of the proofing of our witness the fact is that he would be talking about him having observed fire from the Old Town. My learned friend asked me specifically if that was the case. He asked me that already the day before yesterday, and I answered that question yesterday afternoon. I told him what would the testimony consist of and that it would also involve the testimony about the fire being observed from the -- from the points in Stari Grad, the fire opened by the Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I've got my notes here. We were given two things, an anti-aircraft gun. No problem what that. Anti-aircraft gun at the entrance. We were told he saw a flash or flashes, and as a result of seeing flashes this witness believed that there were -- that there was a mortar, from seeing flashes. There was nothing about mortars. There was nothing about mortars on -- a mortar on the Stari Grad -- I'm sorry, a mortar on the Stradun. That's outside the scope of discovery that -- of disclosure that we've been supplied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if my colleague had allowed me to put my question fully to this witness, he would have received the answers to the questions he's interested in. Unfortunately, he wasn't patient enough. What I told him and what I was told by the witness was that he observed flashes, but I think it's better not for me to testify but, rather, that we ask the witness, for him to tell us what he saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, I think the best course for the moment is to allow the witness to detail what he says he saw, all this evidence being heard at the moment subject to a ruling on your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, first of all, slowly and carefully tell us what firing positions did you observe outside the walls of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: Outside the walls of the Old Town, as I have said, I saw a mortar, an 82-millimetre mortar at the edge of the tennis courts to the left of hotel Lokrum. That is outside the walls. And within the walls --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Slowly, please. First tell us which hotel are you talking about. You said hotel Lokrum?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. Hotel Libertas. Libertas. This is behind the Old Town towards the Petka point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any other firing position outside the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I did not. You mean fire coming, firing?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now tell us, slowly, what did you observe in terms of fire coming from within the Old Town walls.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I observed artillery pieces which I could see with my own eyes, a mortar to the left of the entrance to the Old Town. To the right on the fort -- just a moment, please. To the right I observed an anti-aircraft gun. I didn't observe any fire coming from them, but I did see the artillery piece. I also observed the fire of a mortar coming from a side-street off the Stradun to the left. As the buildings are tall, they were in shadow, so the flashes were clearly visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When we're talking about this mortar, what exactly did you see?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: I saw a flash. The flash was continuous throughout the period of action, with interruptions, of course, when it was fired at.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us more specifically where you observed those flashes that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: As I already said, my view was exactly in the same direction as the Stradun. It was parallel to the Stradun. Halfway along the Stradun, in one of those side-streets to the left between two high buildings the flashes could be seen on the walls of the building from where the fire was coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have another 10 or 15 minutes of questions for this witness, so I am waiting your instructions as to how we should proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We can't finish today because of the time. That is the extent of the evidence you would propose to be admitted from this witness about firing from Dubrovnik on the Old Town, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That is the only topic that remains to be covered, and that will end the testimony of this witness, the examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I asked whether that was the extent of the evidence you propose to lead on this topic of firing from Dubrovnik and the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are positions from which the fire came, and then through the questions I should like to look into some other matters of relevance. We've now discussed the positions, the locations, and now I would address certain other circumstances connected to that fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Weiner, your objection. Do you say that this evidence went beyond that of which you had notice?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, with regard to one mortar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that mortar was?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The mortar to the left of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The one from which the witness did not see any firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All right. And the point of your objection is?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's a disclosure violation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, I would like to say that this is a mortar that was not in the Old Town. It was at the entrance, and I think it is important to note that. As for the rest, it had to do with the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Of your questioning, it came out in response to a question about what did you see firing from within the Old Town. So that you're saying that was misleading, are you, and really it was a mortar at the entrance but not within the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in answer to a question from me about the Old Town, the witness said something that doesn't really apply to the Old Town itself, but that is beyond my control, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you clarify with the witness whether this mortar which he observed but from which he did not see any firing, whether it was within or without the Old Town as he saw it. We've got a couple of minutes left on the tape if you could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, the mortar that you observed near to the entrance, was it within the city walls or right next to the entrance to the town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC
utterances.text: There's the regular entrance to the Old Town and to the left of it right next to the wall of the Old Town. It is outside the walls, between the sea and the wall of the Old Town. That is where the mortar was that I observed. And it moved from that point where I observed it to an area where it disappeared, which meant that it was within the wall, but it was in shadow and I couldn't see it well after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's as much as I can do to clarify the point and the testimony of this witness regarding that particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. A ruling will be given in respect of the evidence about that one weapon in the morning. Thank you. We will adjourn now. Now I must ask you if you would, Captain, to return tomorrow, and we'll continue at 9.00 in the morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.
